newsitem.title: USA: Chretien urges U.S. to resist isolationism.
newsitem.headline: Chretien urges U.S. to resist isolationism.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Wednesday urged the United States to resist isolationism and unilateralism and work with its northern neighbour to promote international security and trade.

"Canada understands the special position of the United States as the only super power in the world today," Chretien said in a speech to the National Press Club. "We recognise the expectations that this creates abroad and the problems it creates domestically.

"But as a friend, we can ony urge that you resist the temptations both of isolationism and sometimes of unilateralism," Chretien added. "We must work together to support continued trade liberalisation and achievement of greater human security, especially among the most impoverished of the world."

As he wound up his two-day vist to Washington, Chretien acknowledged that the two countries had their differences, particularly over policy toward Cuba and a U.S. law aimed at discouraging investment in Cuba. He said those differences were few in a relationship marked mostly by common accord.

But trade relations between the two countries have been strained by fears of North Dakota farmers that Canadian wheat will flood into their markets. The United States has been monitoring Canadian wheat imports since quotas expired in 1995.

Chretien tried to put the dispute in a more positive light. During a question and answer session, he said he thought pasta makers in the United States preferred Canadian durum wheat to make their products.
"So I said to the president of the United States, you have a choice between your farmers and your Italians," Chretien quipped. "So we are selling less durum wheat."
